title: Composable tool graphs: SDK primitives and local simulation (wip)
content:
Goal
Provide a pragmatic SDK surface that lets app engineers compose multiple tool calls (sync + streaming) into a single declarative graph, run and debug that graph locally with faithful simulation of Hosted API behaviours, and get deterministic structured outputs for downstream parsing and testing.

Context & why this matters
- Many integrations today are ad-hoc: single tool calls, or app-side orchestration. Complex features (multi-step retrieval, tool fallback, compositional answers) require coordination that is error-prone and hard to test.
- We want to encourage server-like tool graphs (think: lightweight DAGs) expressed from client code in an ergonomically simple way so teams can iterate locally before deploying to Hosted API.

Design principles
- Composability: small primitives (call, stream, map, fanout, reduce, guard) that can be composed into linear or branching graphs.
- Predictable outputs: each node declares a structured schema/contract (json-schema-lite) for outputs so the root result is validate-able and typeable in client code.
- Local parity: local simulator should replicate latency patterns, partial-stream frames, tool errors, and resilient fallback behaviour so unit/e2e tests catch UX regressions.
- Minimal cognitive load: default behaviours that cover 80% of cases; explicit escape hatches for advanced users.

Surface sketch (pseudo-API)
- Graph.from([
    call('search', {q}),
    stream('generator', {prompt}).map(block => extractActions(block)),
    fanout('enrich', items => items.map(item => call('kb-lookup', {id: item.id})))
  ])
- Each primitive attaches metadata: {timeoutMs, retryPolicy, fallbackTo: 'light-weight-model', outputSchema: '{...}'}
- Streaming nodes emit incremental frames tagged with {nodeId, seq, partial, op}; client runtimes assemble into node-level partials and expose event hooks for UI.

Local simulator features (MVP)
- Declarative tool stubs: allow devs to register local handlers for named tools; support recorded responses for offline tests.
- Stream replay: canned frame sequences (with simulated inter-frame delays) and a small DSL for introducing mid-stream errors or network hiccups.
- Deterministic random seeds for model text generation so tests are reproducible.
- Telemetry shim that can emit the same events the cloud does (timings, token counts, fallback triggers) to local log sink.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How opinionated about graph expressivity? (full Turing-complete workflow vs. small declarative DAG surface)
- Where should structured schemas live? (inline per-node vs. centralized registry with versioning)
- Policy for streaming partial validation: do we validate partial frames against schema or only final assembled output?
- Cost visibility: how do we surface per-node estimated cost in the SDK during local runs?

Backward compatibility and migration
- Provide adapters to convert existing ad-hoc multi-call code to the graph API incrementally. Example: wrap legacy code in a single call node whose handler delegates to older primitives.
- Offer a linter that flags non-deterministic constructs (random seeds, time-based branching) to help testability.

Implementation milestones (Q1-ish roadmap)
- Week 1–2: API sketch + internal feedback sessions (PD, DX, Applied ML)
- Week 3–6: Prototype SDK (JS/TS) with in-process simulator, 3 sample tool stubs, and basic streaming frame model
- Week 7–10: End-to-end demo: user submits graph to Hosted API; server executes with telemetry and structured root output validated against schema; include migration example from an existing app
- Week 11–12: Docs, quickstart, and small playbook for Solutions Eng to use with pilot customers

Notes to self / quick todos
- Sync with serving-runtime on frame wire format (nodeId/op/seq) – Rohit
- Draft minimal json-schema-lite spec for node outputs – Maya
- Prep demo app: email summarizer that splits, searches, enriches, synthesizes final answer with streaming progress – Jon

Inbox links / references
- Slack thread: #prod-hosted-sdk "tool-graphs-proposal" (Dec 01 thread)
- Related PRD: progressive-results-declarative-plugins (see linked_artifacts)

Rough UX scenarios
- Mobile chat UI: show progressive synthesis blocks as streaming nodes finish; if a heavy enrichment node times out, show graceful degradation using cached lightweight model output.
- Analytics: surface per-node latency histogram and fallback counts in Console so product teams can tune batching/quantization per-node.

This doc is intentionally lightweight — aim is to get feedback on the dev ergonomics and the local simulation story. After alignment we'll expand into a formal PRD with wire formats, SDK surface reference, and migration checklist.
